narrativeReportMd:
# Age R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
No local hard instance-breaking change was found for `Age`. The R4 and R6 StructureDefinitions have the same canonical identity, element list, cardinalities, datatypes, modifier flags, summary flags, primary age-unit binding, and Age-specific FHIRPath invariant.

## Scope
The report is scoped to local `Age` changes. Inherited `Quantity`, `Element`, and `DataType` changes are excluded from `findings[]`; the most important inherited issue is the R6 `Quantity.comparator` code `ad`, which can affect Age instances but should be owned by the `Quantity` analysis.

## Main migration themes
Instance data generally does not need an Age-specific transform. Tooling that consumes StructureDefinitions should update its R4 handling of the Age maximum unit value set from the R4 `elementdefinition-maxValueSet` extension to the R6 `ElementDefinition.binding.additional` representation. Terminology code membership for the common age units appears unchanged, but display strings and conformance status changed.

## Highest-impact findings
There are no Critical or High local findings. The only local finding is a Low-impact StructureDefinition metadata conversion risk around the maximum unit binding representation.

## Findings requiring human review
No finding requires human review. Reviewers should still check inherited `Quantity` findings when planning Age migration because they can affect runtime validators and R6-to-R4 conversion of Age values.

## Backward-compatible design observations
The R6 metadata form appears to formalize an R4 extension rather than change the Age value domain. Keeping the old extension in parallel could have helped older tooling, but the instance-level semantics are preserved.

## Follow-up analysis
Analyze `Quantity` for inherited comparator and invariant changes, and use terminology expansion if precise UCUM time-unit coverage is needed.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: No local hard instance-breaking change was found for `Age`. The main migration concern is a Low-impact StructureDefinition metadata representation change for the maximum unit value set; inherited `Quantity` changes, especially comparator code `ad`, must be reviewed separately. Confidence is high for StructureDefinition deltas and medium for terminology expansion effects because no expansions were supplied.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Age instance payloads remain structurally stable: the same elements, cardinalities, primitive types, modifier and summary flags, and local positivity/time-unit invariant are present. Migration work is mostly in validators and model tooling: update R6 StructureDefinition readers to understand `binding.additional[purpose=maximum]`, do not infer an Age-local comparator change, and keep inherited Quantity migration rules separate.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for local StructureDefinition comparison because both assigned StructureDefinitions were present and their snapshots and differentials were compared. Confidence is lower for exhaustive terminology semantics because the supplied ValueSets did not include expansions, especially for the UCUM-filtered `all-time-units` maximum value set.

findings.title: Age maximum unit value set moved from R4 maxValueSet extension to R6 binding.additional

oldState.summary: The root Age binding used extensible ValueSet/age-units and represented the maximum permitted unit set with the R4 elementdefinition-maxValueSet extension.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The primary age-unit ValueSet compose was compared and contains the same UCUM codes in R4 and R6. The maximum all-time-units ValueSet compose was also the same, but no expansion was available.

oldState.narrativeMd: In R4, the Age differential carries `binding.valueSet = http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/age-units` and an extension `http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/elementdefinition-maxValueSet` pointing at `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/all-time-units`.

newState.summary: The root Age binding keeps the same extensible primary ValueSet but represents the maximum unit set with ElementDefinition.binding.additional purpose maximum.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: R6 keeps the same primary age-units ValueSet URL and uses `binding.additional[{purpose: maximum}]` for all-time-units.

newState.narrativeMd: In R6, the same maximum value set is expressed as `binding.additional` with `purpose = maximum` and `valueSet = http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/all-time-units`.

facts.note: The primary extensible binding identity did not change.
R4 used an extension to express the maximum binding.
R6 uses the core additional binding structure.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The same root `Age` element and same value-set URLs are present in both versions; only the metadata representation of the maximum binding changed.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This does not make an R4 Age instance invalid in R6: the primary extensible binding and maximum value-set URL are preserved. The risk is for validators, code generators, or conformance tooling that read the raw StructureDefinition. R4-specific tools that only search for the `elementdefinition-maxValueSet` extension can miss the R6 maximum binding; R6-to-R4 metadata conversion must map `binding.additional[purpose=maximum]` back to the R4 extension if an R4-shaped StructureDefinition is required.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The likely failure mode is under- or over-enforcement of acceptable Age units by tooling, not loss of clinical Age values in normal instance exchange.

justification.inferredGoal: Promote a formerly extension-based maximum binding into the standard R6 ElementDefinition binding model.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: R6 could have retained the R4 maxValueSet extension alongside `binding.additional` as deprecated transition metadata.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal is reasonable: move the maximum binding from an R4 extension convention into the first-class R6 `ElementDefinition.binding.additional` model. This does not change the Age instance value domain, but it can break metadata consumers that only know the R4 `elementdefinition-maxValueSet` extension. A dual-representation transition was available, so the break was not the only possible design; however, the affected surface is low-impact tooling metadata and the alternative carries real duplication and cleanup costs. On balance, the change is probably justified rather than clearly avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base R6 design would have emitted both `binding.additional[purpose=maximum]` and the legacy `http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/elementdefinition-maxValueSet` extension on the Age root binding for a transition period. That would let many R4-era validators and code generators keep finding the maximum value set while R6-aware tools used the native field. The alternative is only partial because it creates two same-resource representations of one semantic fact, requires consistency checks, and could leave the legacy extension in active use indefinitely instead of completing the move to the core R6 binding model.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: This would improve compatibility for legacy StructureDefinition tooling but duplicate the same maximum-binding fact and require synchronization, risking indefinite extension support.

evidence.detail: R4 Age uses elementdefinition-maxValueSet to identify the maximum time-unit ValueSet.
R6 Age uses binding.additional with purpose maximum for the same ValueSet.
The primary binding remains extensible to ValueSet/age-units.
The primary binding remains extensible to ValueSet/age-units.

examples.examplesMd: The example is a StructureDefinition binding metadata transform, not an Age instance transform.

findings.narrativeMd: The Age-specific unit binding semantics are preserved, but the way the maximum allowable unit set is represented changed. This matters for validators and code generators that inspect StructureDefinition JSON rather than using a version-aware FHIR model. An R4-only reader may look for the R4 extension and conclude that R6 Age has no maximum binding unless it is updated to read `binding.additional`.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: There is no old-valid/new-invalid Age instance solely because of this change. Correct R6 validation should still apply the same primary extensible age-unit binding and the same maximum all-time-units concept. The compatibility issue is metadata-level: R6 StructureDefinition content is not naively R4-shaped, and an R6-to-R4 StructureDefinition conversion must translate the additional binding back to the R4 extension to preserve validation semantics.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Update validators, code generators, and StructureDefinition conversion scripts to map R4 `elementdefinition-maxValueSet` and R6 `binding.additional[purpose=maximum]` as equivalent facts. Add tests that read both R4 and R6 Age definitions and verify that the maximum value-set URL remains `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/all-time-units`.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change was likely part of a general R6 improvement to make additional bindings first-class. A backward-compatible alternative would have been to emit both the new core representation and the old extension for at least one release, but that would duplicate metadata and require consistency checks.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The change is confined to how the Age root binding records its maximum value set in the StructureDefinition. R4 used the `elementdefinition-maxValueSet` extension and R6 uses `binding.additional` with `purpose` = `maximum`, but both point to `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/all-time-units` and the primary extensible binding to `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/age-units` remains. That can require R6-aware conformance tooling, but it does not make an R4-valid Age instance invalid in R6 and does not change the Age value, unit, system, code, or local age invariant semantics.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition-Age differential root binding has `strength: extensible`, `valueSet: http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/age-units`, and extension `elementdefinition-maxValueSet` = `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/all-time-units`.

R6 StructureDefinition-Age root binding keeps `strength: extensible` and `valueSet: http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/age-units`, and represents the same maximum value set as `binding.additional[{purpose: maximum, valueSet: http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/all-time-units}]`.
The R4 and R6 Age root constraint `age-1` has the same computable expression requiring a code when value exists, UCUM system when system exists, and positive value.
R4 input context says trial-use; the R4 StructureDefinition also carries standards-status `trial-use`.
freshReview.fmmEffect: The supplied R4 maturity/status context is trial-use rather than normative, so it does not heighten stability expectations. In any case, maturity is not decisive here because the compatibility mechanism is metadata/tooling only and the underlying instance conformance meaning is preserved.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: metadata/tooling: raw StructureDefinition readers that only understand the R4 maximum-value-set extension must learn the R6 additional-binding representation, but normal Age instances and validators using R6 metadata are not broken.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking representation for legacy metadata consumers would be to duplicate the old `elementdefinition-maxValueSet` extension alongside `binding.additional`, but that would preserve a superseded representation and create redundant fields that could drift. The R6 base design keeps the same semantics in the standard additional-binding slot, which is appropriate for a metadata schema evolution.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing low-impact/no-hard-break assessment and with the absence of a meaningful less-breaking alternative; the fresh review frames the concern as metadata/tooling rather than instance compatibility.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: `Age` remains `http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/Age`, id `Age`, kind `complex-type`, type `Age`, non-abstract, and a specialization of `Quantity`.
Both snapshots contain the same eight element ids: `Age`, `Age.id`, `Age.extension`, `Age.value`, `Age.comparator`, `Age.unit`, `Age.system`, and `Age.code`.
All local and inherited snapshot min/max cardinalities match between R4 and R6 for the Age snapshot.

The element type codes are unchanged: `decimal` for `Age.value`, `code` for `Age.comparator` and `Age.code`, `string` for `Age.unit`, `uri` for `Age.system`, `Extension` for `Age.extension`, and FHIRPath string for `Age.id`.
`Age` has no Reference-typed elements or targetProfile lists.

The local root binding strength and primary value-set URL are unchanged, and the age-units compose contains the same six UCUM codes. The maximum all-time-units binding URL is also unchanged, but its StructureDefinition representation changed and is reported separately.

The Age-local invariant `age-1` keeps severity `error`, the same human text, and the same FHIRPath expression requiring a code when value exists, UCUM system when system exists, and positive value when value is present. New or changed inherited Quantity/Element constraints are out of scope.
No Age element has a fixed, pattern, or default value in either version.
No minValue, maxValue, maxLength, or regex limit changed. Positivity remains enforced through the unchanged `age-1` FHIRPath invariant.
`Age.comparator` remains a modifier, and the other Age snapshot elements keep their modifier status.
Summary flags are unchanged for the Age snapshot elements.
No slicing is present on Age elements in either version.
The Age short and definition text are unchanged. Top-level description wording drops the R4 boilerplate prefix `Base StructureDefinition for`, which does not change conformance semantics.
No Age instance JSON/XML element serialization change was found. StructureDefinition metadata serialization changed for the maximum binding and is captured as the local finding.

No local Age element was added that would make R6 Age instances unrepresentable in R4. The inherited R6 `Quantity.comparator` code `ad` can create an R6-to-R4 representability issue for Age instances, but that is owned by the `Quantity` analysis.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Age conformance maturity/status advanced
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R4 `Age` has StructureDefinition status `draft` and standards-status `trial-use`; R6 has status `active` and standards-status `normative`. This does not change instance shape or validation rules.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Governance, documentation, and conformance tooling may treat R6 Age as more stable. Do not interpret this as a local data transform requirement.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Common age-unit codes stayed the same but displays and ValueSet status changed
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Both R4 and R6 `ValueSet/age-units` include the same UCUM codes `min`, `h`, `d`, `wk`, `mo`, and `a`. R6 changes displays from plural words to UCUM-style singular/abbreviated displays and changes ValueSet status from draft to active; membership is unchanged.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Systems that compare or regenerate display text may see changed labels. Validation should key on system and code, not display.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Age-local invariant keeps the same FHIRPath while R4 XPath metadata is absent in R6
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The Age-local invariant `age-1` has the same severity, human text, and FHIRPath expression in both versions, so the intended validation rule is unchanged. R6 no longer carries the R4 XPath expression in the constraint component.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: XPath-only validation tooling should migrate to the FHIRPath expression. Note that the R4 XPath text used `>=0` while the R4 and R6 FHIRPath expression uses `> 0`, so tools relying on the old XPath may already have differed from the computable FHIRPath rule.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Root RIM mapping was simplified
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The R4 root Age element had two RIM mapping entries, including a terse `PQ` entry. R6 keeps the more descriptive RIM mapping and drops the duplicate terse entry. These mappings are informative metadata and do not affect instance validation.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Mapping-documentation generators may produce slightly different root mapping output, but no Age instance conversion rule was removed from the computable element model.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: `Age` specializes `Quantity`; inherited R6 changes include the required comparator value set adding code `ad`, the inherited best-practice warning `qty-4`, and the `Quantity` baseDefinition moving through `DataType`. These can affect Age validators and R6-to-R4 conversion but are not local Age findings.
